boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the Nitro SDK's os_irqTable.c, 0x02056c40..0x02056d64: 10 functions. pret/pokediamond's arm9/lib/NitroSDK/src/OS_irqTable.c, compiled with its own pinned mwccarm 1.2/sp2p3, emits OSi_IrqTimer3..0 (0x10 each), OSi_IrqDma3..0 (0x10 each), OSi_IrqCallback 0x9c and OS_IrqDummy 0x4; the run here has the same ten in the same order, with OSi_IrqCallback (DmaTimHandler) at 0xa0. No function in the run is unexplained.
TOP EDGE: ClearInterrupts at 0x02056d64 is OS_ResetRequestIrqMask, the first function of os_interrupt.c (arm9/OS_Interrupt); OS_IrqDummy (EmptyHandler, 0x02056d60) is os_irqTable.c's last.
BOTTOM EDGE: Copy48BytesFixed at 0x02056c1c..0x02056c40 is a hand-assembled MI block-copy primitive, not interrupt code.
Split from the former arm9/IRQ, which held both SDK files in one TU because its members share the IRQ:: namespace.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows arm9/GX_VramCnt.

The coined IRQ:: members now carry their SDK names from pret/pokediamond OS_irqTable.c (OS_IrqDummy, OSi_IrqCallback, OSi_IrqDma0-3, OSi_IrqTimer0-3) with C linkage, declared in include/nitro/os/interrupt.h.
Text-only: os_irqTable.c's tables (the IE handler table OS_IRQTable, the IE-bit index table OSi_IrqCallbackInfoIndex and the callback table OSi_IrqCallbackInfo) are not claimed here.
